THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 06.03.2018 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.741/2017.
This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under;
That on 13.08.2016 at about 10.55 a.m., one Imthiyaz Ahmed @ Imthiyaz Pasha S/o. Abdul Kareem was walking as a pedestrian on the left side of the road at Shivaji road, Shivajinagar met with an accident being hit NC: 2024:KHC:1936 by the bullet motor cycle bearing registration No.08A- 0596741L, which was ridden by the rider of the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner. Due to the impact of the said accident, the said Imthiyaz Ahmed fell down and sustained grievous injures.

Immediately, he was shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital at Shivajinagar and thereafter, to NIMHANS hospital for better treatment, but he succumbed to the injuries, before reaching the NIMHANS hospital.
Due to the occurrence of the accident, a crime came to be registered in Crime No.287/2016 against the rider of the motor cycle.
3.1 It is stated that prior to the occurrence of accident, deceased Imthiyaz Ahmed was hale and healthy, aged about 48 years, working as Auto Top Cover Layer and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The claimants, who are the children and mother of the deceased were wholly dependant upon the earnings of the deceased Imthiyaz Ahmed.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
On service of notice, respondent remained absent and he was placed Ex parte.

sentences.text: On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 was examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P11.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submission of learned counsel for claimants, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.6,54,000/- with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization and respondent being the insurer was directed to deposit the amount within two months.
3.6 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the tribunal has committed serious error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation and assessed the income of the deceased on the lower side.

It is contended that the tribunal has failed to award future prospects at 25% as contemplated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 and also committed an error by deducting 50% of income of deceased towards personal expenses instead of 1/3rd, as there are three dependants of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended that under the head loss of consortium, the tribunal has not awarded just and reasonable compensation.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation and to allow the appeal preferred by the claimants.
5. Per contra, Sri Bheemaiah, learned counsel representing respondent-Insurance Company primarily NC: 2024:KHC:1936 contends that the notice was not served to the respondent.
The involvement of the vehicle also is in question.
Assessment made by the tribunal with regard to compensation is correct and the same does not call for interference.

It is also contended by the learned counsel for respondent that the tribunal has rightly deducted 50% towards personal and living expenses as deceased had one dependent and other two children were adults and capable of earning and maintaining themselves.
He further contends that under other heads also the tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
He also contends that the tribunal has awarded an interest at 8% p.a., which is also on the higher side.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for appellants- claimants and learned counsel for respondent,
perused the judgment and award passed by the tribunal, it is seen that the accident occurred on 13.08.2016.
Deceased was a NC: 2024:KHC:1936 pedestrian on the left side of the road, rider of the motor cycle dashed against the deceased, due to which deceased fell down and died on the way to hospital.

In order to substantiate these aspects, the claimants have produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P11, out of which, Exs.P1 to P7 are the police records and Exs.P8 to P11 are the records to show the age for assessment of compensation.

Filing of the FIR and laying of charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle is not in dispute and not challenged, whereby it can be said that the rider Smt. Seema vs Union Of India on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135084354/
3 of the motor cycle has accepted the charges laid against him.
Therefore, the negligence is rightly attributed against the rider of the motor cycle.
As on the date of occurrence of accident, deceased was aged 48 years.
To establish the same, Ex.P8-voter ID is produced by the claimants.
The tribunal has taken the age of the deceased to be 50 years, at the time of accident, the same does not call for interference.
The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '13', which does not call for interference.
Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of the deceased, the tribunal having assessed the age to be 50 years and the multiplier at '13',
which does not call for interference.
The income taken by the tribunal is Rs.8,000/- per month as notional income, no documentary proof is produced before the tribunal to show the income.
However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.9,500/- for the accident of the year 2016.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.9,500/-.
The tribunal has failed to add 25% towards future prospects, which requires to be added in the present case for computation of compensation.
The tribunal has deducted 50% towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

However, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, the deceased is a married person having 2 to 3 dependents and the tribunal ought to have taken 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses.

sentences.text: Accordingly, in this case also 1/3rd is taken as deduction.
Therefore, the income shall be taken as Rs.7,917/- (Rs.9,500/- + 25% - 1/3rd).
Hence, loss of dependency would be Rs.12,35,052/- (Rs.7,917/- x 12 x 13) as against Rs.6,24,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
8. The tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head consortium.

As there are three dependents, each would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- per head as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 followed by Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs.
Nanu Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

Though learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that the interest awarded by - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:1936 the tribunal is on the higher side, it is also to be noted that the respondent has not preferred appeal questioning the judgment and award of the tribunal nor cross objections in this appeal.
Under the circumstances, the appellants- claimants cannot be put into worst situation for having approached this Court.
Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum;
